verdict.rationale: Weave's docs say users can evaluate responses with LLM judges and custom scorers. Custom scorers can be function-based or class-based, and a guide describes scoring agents with an LLM judge, so the core LLM-as-a-judge capability is first-party. The evidence does not show how the judge itself is configured, such as its model, prompt or rubric, and nothing independent corroborates it. missing for 10: explicit documentation of configurable judge model/prompt/rubric settings, independent or hands-on corroboration of LLM-judge scoring.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can score outputs with configurable LLM-as-a-judge evaluators

citations.quote: Evaluate your agent’s or application’s responses using LLM judges and custom scorers
Evaluate single-turn and multi-turn AI agents in Weave using the agents workflow and EvaluationLogger, scored with an LLM judge.
Class-based Scorers: Python classes that inherit from weave.Scorer for more complex evaluations.
Custom Scorers let you encode evaluation criteria that are specific to your use case, beyond what the built-in Scorers cover.
